audit.whatIsWrong: Purgatory (R) was treated only as an execute zone. Two of its properties never appear anywhere on the page: it is a PROJECTILE, and it GROUNDS.
audit.why: The kit carries both flags on R — projectile and grounding — plus slow, execute and zone. That makes it the single most important interaction in the lane for Yasuo specifically: Wind Wall deletes the throw outright, and if it does land, grounding shuts off Sweeping Blade, the Steel Tempest dash and Last Breath. The page instead asserted 'the totem cannot execute a Yasuo mid-ult', which is not in Riot's text and I could not verify.
audit.corrected: Purgatory is a thrown projectile Wind Wall blocks; if it lands it grounds you and your dashes are gone.

audit.whatIsWrong: All seven rows gave the stage to Yasuo against a 49.95% win rate over 2100 games.
audit.why: A sweep of the chart cannot coexist with a coin-flip win rate. The page's own first-item row was already the lowest-rated (6/10) and its text says 'respect the all-in until his E is down' — that is not a row you own. His Lich Bane spike also lands before a crit item completes.
audit.corrected: First item row to Skill on both layers, rating to 5/10, with matching prose. Remaining rows left as-is; there is no mirror audit for this matchup yet.

audit.whatIsWrong: The level 6 and first-item spike text described the wrong mechanism.
audit.why: Level 6 matters because of the grounding projectile, not because of a claimed ult-juggle immunity. First item matters because Lich Bane arrives before your crit spike.
audit.corrected: phases[4].why, phases[5].why, whys[5] and spikes[1].text rewritten around the verified mechanics.

audit.whatIsWrong: Itemization said 'Anti-heal is optional — his sustain is self-refund, not lifesteal.'
audit.why: Riot's text for Soul Ignition: 'Locke will heal back a portion of the damage he takes during the effect.' That is healing, and Grievous Wounds reduces healing regardless of its source. Calling it optional tells the user to skip the item that beats his entire sustain pattern on an 18s cycle.
audit.corrected: Executioner's Calling is not optional here; it cuts the Soul Ignition refund.

audit.whatIsWrong: The 'blink-bite' was described without the auto-attack reset that makes it work.
audit.why: Ashen Pursuit (E) carries the autoReset flag — the wind-up as he lands is the cue to step back, not the cast.

edits.before: Lich Bane spike — his blink-bite now genuinely one-shots marked squishies. Respect the all-in until his E is down.
edits.after: Lich Bane spike — his blink-bite one-shots marked targets. This row is his: hold Wind Wall for the R, farm to item two.

edits.before: First crit item spikes your autos past his W burst window.
edits.after: His Lich Bane lands before your crit item; it is even here.

edits.before: Purgatory changes the rules: fights now end at HIS floor — disengage above ~15% or leave the totem zone entirely.
edits.after: Purgatory grounds you and executes low targets — but it is a projectile, so hold Wind Wall for the throw, not for his nails.

edits.before: One landed knockup ends him: Last Breath juggles him through his own R Purgatory window and the totem cannot execute a Yasuo mid-ult - all-in freely off any Q3.
edits.after: Purgatory is a thrown projectile - Wind Wall eats it outright, and if it lands it grounds you, so your E and Q dashes are gone. Wall it, then all-in off any Q3.

edits.before: Wind Wall timed on his Q nail volleys
edits.after: Wind Wall his Q volleys and his R throw

edits.before: R Purgatory placed while your R is down
edits.after: R Purgatory landing to ground your dashes

edits.before: E is his engage AND escape — a spent blink is the lane’s biggest cooldown; don’t waste yours before it.
edits.after: E is a 10s blink that resets his attack — the wind-up as he lands is your cue to step back, not the cast.

edits.before: Track Locke’s Ritual Nails (Marks): The nail marks are his whole engine — without 2-3 stacks on you his blink-in barely dents; sidestep the recasts and punish the ten seconds of nothing. Commit only while it is down.
edits.after: Track Locke's Ritual Nails (Marks): without 2-3 stacks his blink-in barely dents. Purgatory (R) is a projectile — Wind Wall deletes it, and if it lands it grounds you, so Sweeping Blade and Steel Tempest cannot move you.

edits.before: Early HP and MR blunt the nail chip (his damage is AP). A stopwatch/Zhonya’s-class answer beats Purgatory outright: untargetable at the floor = execute denied. Anti-heal is optional — his sustain is self-refund, not lifesteal.
edits.after: Early HP and MR blunt the nail chip (his damage is AP). Executioner's Calling is not optional — Soul Ignition refunds a portion of the self-damage he takes, and Grievous Wounds cuts that refund on an 18s cycle.

notes: No mirror exists for this matchup yet, so a Locke-side audit should restate: Purgatory is a projectile Wind Wall blocks, and grounding is the counter to Yasuo's whole kit (E, the Q dash, and Last Breath). UNVERIFIED and left alone: the page calls his Q 'Ritual Nails' while Riot's text says he 'readies a set of Soul Nails to throw' — that may be the ability name versus the thrown object, and I had no source to settle it, so I did not touch the name anywhere. Also unverified: the '125-range' figure used in phases[0].why and breakdown.wave — his attack range is not in the kit file. The W trueDamage flag looks like a tooltip-parse misfire (the only damage described is self-damage), so I made no claim from it.
